== con-leche/ConLeche/MainTheorem.lean#L96-L124
    96  /-- **The main theorem.**  Every environment the checker accepts has a
    97  model in every set theory — at every `Nat.div`/`Nat.mod` pin list, so
    98  consistency does not depend on which variants the install gate is
    99  handed (the empty list included: under it every stream that declares
   100  `Nat.div` declines).  The shipped binary runs the fold at
   101  `natOpPinSets`. -/
   102  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
   103      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (maxNatSize : Nat) (ds : Array Declaration) (env : Env)
   104      (accepted : checkDecls .verified pins maxNatSize ds = .ok env) :
   105      Nonempty (Model V env) := by
   106    obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) accepted
   107    exact ⟨Model.Model.ofEnvModelM m⟩
   108  
   109  open Frontend in
   110  /-- **The main corollary.**  A file declaring a theorem of type `False`
   111  in the shape `jsonWithTheoremFalse` describes is rejected: the parse
   112  reads the template's four lines into a theorem record of type `False`,
   113  the preparation keeps the record, and a stream holding it is never
   114  accepted.  At every pin list, as the main theorem: the shipped binary
   115  runs the fold at `natOpPinSets`. -/
   116  theorem no_False_declaration (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
   117      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (maxNatSize : Nat) (chunks : List ByteArray)
   118      (h : jsonWithTheoremFalse chunks) :
   119      ∃ e, (do
   120        let pre ← builtinPreludeE
   121        let r ← parseChunks chunks
   122        let ds := preparePrelude pre r.decls
   123        checkDecls .verified pins maxNatSize ds) = .error e := by
   124    refine Except.exists_error_of_not_ok fun env hacc => ?_

== con-leche/ConLeche/Verify/Cached/MainC.lean#L33-L39
    33  /-- **Acceptance**: what the fold accepts carries the model. -/
    34  theorem checkDecls_sound
    35      {ds : Array Declaration} {env' : Env}
    36      (h : checkDecls .verified pins maxNatSize ds = .ok env') :
    37      Nonempty (EnvModelM V env') := by
    38    obtain ⟨n, fe, r, rfl⟩ := checkDecls_run .verified h
    39    exact (declsRun_model (V := V) r rfl ConLeche.Model.EnvModelOk.empty).nonempty

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L13
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```

   112    --verified          Check in the mode the soundness theorem covers (default)
   113    --trusted           Skip the checks only the proof needs; outside the theorem
   114    --jobs=N            Worker threads (default: one per hardware thread, at most 16)
   115    --max-nat-size=N    Largest Nat numeral in bytes the checker takes in or
   116                        computes; a larger one is rejected (default 134217728)
   117    --progress[=PACE]   Report progress on stderr: PACE is N declarations
   118                        (default 1), P% of each phase, or Ss seconds
   119    --pins FILE         Testing only: check with this Nat pin list instead of
   120                        the embedded one (outside the theorems)
   121    --no-pins           Testing only: check with no Nat pin list
   122    --help              Print this help and exit
   123    --                  End of options
   124  
   125  .olean input:
   126    --olean             Read modules and their import closure from .olean files
   127    --search-path=DIRS  Colon-separated .olean directories; repeatable
   128    --constant=NAME     Check only NAME and what it mentions; repeatable
   129  
   130  Exit status:
   131    0  accepted
   132    1  rejected: a declaration is invalid
   133    2  declined: an unsupported feature
   134    3  error: bad usage, malformed input or an internal failure
   135  
   136  Documentation:
   137    README.md and OVERVIEW.md of the con-ron repository";

    18  //! | exit | verdict | meaning |
    19  //! |---|---|---|
    20  //! | 0 | `accepted N declarations` | every declaration checked; `N` counts the file's declaration records |

    22  //! | 2 | `declined` | the checker positively detected a feature it does not support, and says which |

== crates/con-ron-core/src/kernel/name.rs#L622-L634
   622  pub fn render(n: &Name) -> Vec<u32> {
   623      match &n.0.kind {
   624          NameKind::Anonymous => {
   625              const A: [u32; 11] = [91, 97, 110, 111, 110, 121, 109, 111, 117, 115, 93];
   626              crate::kernel::core_types::code_points(&A)
   627          }
   628          _ => {
   629              let cs = component_list(n, Vec::new());
   630              let k = cs.len();
   631              display_acc_finish(render_from(&cs, k, display_acc_empty()))
   632          }
   633      }
   634  }

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L14-L85
    14  /-!
    15  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    16  
    17  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    18  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    19  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    20  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's headline theorems:
    21  
    22  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — the environment of every stream the Aeneas
    23    model of the Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    24  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    25    type `False` is never accepted by it;
    26  * `no_False_oleans` / `model_exists_oleans` — the same on `--olean`.
    27  
    28  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    29  frontier is measured as their dependency closure, and §5's census prints their
    30  axioms.  What they assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    31  
    32  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    33  
    34  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    35  around the extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    36  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    37  
    38      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    39        → prepare_d → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the check phase)
    40  
    41  **The check phase is the one the binary's driver runs, pool and all**
    42  (`driver::check_decls_driver`): it builds the stream's index from the records
    43  (`stream_index::build_index`), freezes the tier with the index in it
    44  (`checker::freeze_tier`), runs every record's job on `pool::parallel_all`, and
    45  thaws the tier.  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` the index, `h7`
    46  the freeze, `h8` the pool), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles into
    47  `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  `h8` is the contract of the generic
    48  combinator `pool::parallel_all` at the driver's two verified closures (`ParallelAll`
    49  at `jobStep`): index lists, one per worker, covering every job, each in increasing
    50  order, and for each a fold of `run_job` over its indices from `worker_state`,
    51  accepting.  That contract is the pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of
    52  `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.
    53  
    54  The proof:
    55  
    56  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s `…_refines` lemmas walk the Rust runs
    57     into twin runs from the twin's own start state `AState.init EStore.empty`,
    58     related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/`AStateInv`: lockstep); `rust_stages`;
    59  2. **Theorem 1** — `Bridge/Stages.lean` takes the twin runs:
    60     `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` makes the check phase's accept con-leche's pure
    61     fold `checkDeclsPure` accepting the denoted stream at `streamEnv` of it;
    62  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a model,
    63     and `no_proof_of_False_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream.
    64  
    65  ## The named hypotheses
    66  
    67  The headlines start from the binary's own start values (`startState` =
    68  `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`) and name the call the
    69  binary makes at each step.  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    70  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`), what
    71  they assume is exactly:
    72  
    73  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks: the binary
    74    parses with the verified reader loop `parse_source` over the driver's file
    75    handle, and `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
    76    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands out
    77    the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam;
    78  * on `--olean`, `hsnap : SnapshotOf finst fsv F` — the file instance answers as
    79    one snapshot `F`.
    80  
    81  `hpins` is the premise for the binary's pin step: the pin list is what the verified
    82  decoder read, at any text (as con-leche's theorems hold at every pin list);
    83  `model_exists_embedded` / `no_False_declaration_embedded` fix the text to the embedded
    84  `PINS_TEXT`.
    85  -/

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L460-L464
   460  def RustDenotes (ds : alloc.vec.Vec arena.env.IDeclaration) (st : arena.monad.AState)
   461      (env : ConLeche.Env) : Prop :=
   462    ∃ (lst : ConRon.Arena.AState) (dsP : List ConLeche.Declaration),

   186  structure SnapshotOf {Fs : Type} (inst : frontend.olean.files.OleanFs Fs) (fsv : Fs)
   187      (F : ConLeche.FS) : Prop where
   188    path_exists : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.path_exists fsv p = ok (.Ok b) →
   189      b = (F.real q).isSome
   190    real_path : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ r, inst.real_path fsv p = ok (.Ok r) →
   191      F.real q = some ⟨ConRon.Refine.absString r⟩ ∧ ConRon.Refine.StrWF r
   192    read_bin_file : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.read_bin_file fsv p = ok (.Ok b) →
   193      F.file q = some (absBytes (alloc.vec.Vec.deref b))
   194    read_range : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ off len b, inst.read_range fsv p off len = ok (.Ok b) →
   195      ∃ whole, F.file q = some whole ∧ absBytes (alloc.vec.Vec.deref b) =
   196        whole.extract off.val (min (off.val + len.val) whole.size)
   197    file_size : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ s, inst.file_size fsv p = ok (.Ok s) →
   198      ∃ whole, F.file q = some whole ∧ s.val = whole.size

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L30
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```
    14  //!
    15  //! (tier 0 = persistent, 1 = scratch; the index is into THAT CONSTRUCTOR'S
    16  //! array of THAT TIER).  The zero word is a narrow handle — tag 0,
    17  //! persistent, slot 0 — which is the twin's `default : Idx k` and every
    18  //! `of_word(0)` below: the anonymous name, the level `zero`, a handle that
    19  //! decodes.  An expression `app` array holds 2^30 = 1 073 741 824 nodes per
    20  //! tier and every other constructor array 2^26 =
    21  //! 67 108 864: apps are 85 % of an export's expression nodes, so they are the
    22  //! array that runs out first, and they get the room.  Only the expression
    23  //! `app` tag is wide — a level `param` handle is narrow although `LTAG_PARAM`
    24  //! has `ETAG_APP`'s value — and `word_tag` reads `ETAG_APP` off a word with
    25  //! bit 30 set, so the tag of a handle is read the same way for all four
    26  //! kinds.
    27  //!
    28  //! The tier is the TOP bit, above both shapes' index, so a persistent
    29  //! handle's bits never change when the scratch tier comes and goes
    30  //! (con-leche's lesson 6).

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3603-L3638
  3603  
  3604      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:482-502 EStore.intern
  3605      /// Hash-cons an expression node: probe the persistent cons table, then the
  3606      /// scratch one, then append to the tier the store is in (DESIGN.md §8.3).
  3607      /// The cap test is the Lean's `capOK` turned into the `Native` decline
  3608      /// §8.3 puts here.
  3609      ///
  3610      /// **Dispatched ONCE** (task #97-P6-15).  The body below used to run the
  3611      /// whole sequence over the `ENodeView`, and each of its four steps
  3612      /// dispatched on the view's tag again and built the node record again:
  3613      /// the persistent probe built it (inside `ETables::find`), the scratch
  3614      /// probe built it a second time, `der_of_view` re-dispatched to compute
  3615      /// the derived word, and `ETables::push` re-dispatched and built it a
  3616      /// third time to append it.  So the tag is read once here and the ten per-constructor
  3617      /// paths below each build their record ONCE and hand the same `&r` to the
  3618      /// two probes, to the capacity test and to the push — the same clauses in
  3619      /// the same order, with the dispatch and the two rebuilds gone.
  3620      ///
  3621      /// The twin's `intern` is one `def` over `ENodeView`; what is owed is the
  3622      /// ten-arm spelling and `internC v = intern (view of C)` per constructor,
  3623      /// each of them `rfl` after the `match`.
  3624      pub fn intern(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, v: ENodeView) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3625          match v {
  3626              ENodeView::BVar(i) => self.intern_bvar(pers, i),
  3627              ENodeView::FVar(idx, ty) => self.intern_fvar(pers, idx, ty),
  3628              ENodeView::Sort(u) => self.intern_sort(pers, u),
  3629              ENodeView::Const(n, us) => self.intern_const(pers, n, us),
  3630              ENodeView::App(f, a) => self.intern_app(pers, f, a),
  3631              ENodeView::Lam(ty, body) => self.intern_lam(pers, ty, body),
  3632              ENodeView::ForallE(ty, body) => self.intern_forall_e(pers, ty, body),
  3633              ENodeView::LetE(ty, val, body) => self.intern_let_e(pers, ty, val, body),
  3634              ENodeView::Lit(l) => self.intern_lit(pers, l),
  3635              ENodeView::Proj(n, i, e) => self.intern_proj(pers, n, i, e),
  3636          }
  3637      }
  3638  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3888-L3935
  3888      pub fn intern_app(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, f: EIdx, a: EIdx) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3889          let r: AppNode = AppNode { f, a };
  3890          let sk: bool = if self.scratch_on {
  3891              if r.f.is_persistent() {
  3892                  !r.a.is_persistent()
  3893              } else {
  3894                  true
  3895              }
  3896          } else {
  3897              false
  3898          };
  3899          let hit: Option<EIdx> = if sk {
  3900              None
  3901          } else if pers.frozen {
  3902              pers.e.apps.find(&r)
  3903          } else {
  3904              self.pers.apps.find(&r)
  3905          };
  3906          match hit {
  3907              Some(hp) => Ok(hp),
  3908              None => {
  3909                  if self.scratch_on {
  3910                      let at: (usize, Option<EIdx>) = self.scr.apps.find_slot(&r);
  3911                      match at.1 {
  3912                          Some(hs) => Ok(hs),
  3913                          None => {
  3914                              if self.scr.apps.full_wide() {
  3915                                  Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3916                              } else {
  3917                                  let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3918                                  let h: EIdx =
  3919                                      EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_S, self.scr.apps.size() as u32);
  3920                                  self.scr.apps.push_at(at.0, r, d, h.dup2());
  3921                                  Ok(h)
  3922                              }
  3923                          }
  3924                      }
  3925                  } else if self.pers.apps.full_wide() {
  3926                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3927                  } else {
  3928                      let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3929                      let h: EIdx = EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_P, self.pers.apps.size() as u32);
  3930                      self.pers.apps.push(r, d, h.dup2());
  3931                      Ok(h)
  3932                  }
  3933              }
  3934          }
  3935      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core.rs#L11843-L11862
 11843  /// con-leche: none — **a job's bracket, closed** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 11844  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:4459-4467 dropScratch` —
 11845  /// the twin's `dropScratch` on a store that STAYS frozen (task #98-FREEZE): the
 11846  /// caches flushed and the scratch tiers emptied, the flag untouched.  A
 11847  /// worker's store is frozen for its whole life, so between two jobs it is
 11848  /// frozen with an empty scratch tier where the twin's is scratch-off; nothing
 11849  /// is interned there.
 11850  pub fn leave_record(st: &mut AState) {
 11851      flush_caches(st);
 11852      st.store.clear_scratch();
 11853  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L65-L88
    65  /// con-leche: none — the phase boundary, which con-leche has no tier to make
    66  /// Lean twin: none — the twin has no tier to move; its worker reads the
    67  /// persistent tier where it is (`AState.worker`, `Arena/Checker.lean`).
    68  /// **The persistent tier and the stream's index into a value**: the four
    69  /// persistent tables and the index move into one `PersTier` handed back
    70  /// `frozen`, for the workers to read (the index is the base `ifenv_find` reads
    71  /// below a job's own layer).  A pure MOVE: the store's scratch tiers and flags
    72  /// are untouched (a worker's store is its own, `worker_state`), and
    73  /// `thaw_tier` puts everything back where it was.  The driver's store is not
    74  /// read between the two.
    75  pub fn freeze_tier(ar: &mut EStore, ix: IStreamIndex) -> PersTier {
    76      let n: NTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.ns.pers, NTables::empty());
    77      let l: LTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.pers, LTables::empty());
    78      let ls: LsTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.pers, LsTables::empty());
    79      let e: ETables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.pers, ETables::empty());
    80      PersTier {
    81          frozen: true,
    82          n,
    83          l,
    84          ls,
    85          e,
    86          env: ix,
    87      }
    88  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L1217-L1269
  1217  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:365-373 EStore
  1218  /// **The persistent tier of all four stores, as one value `n` phase-B workers
  1219  /// read by reference** — DESIGN.md §8.3's "the persistent tier is immutable in
  1220  /// phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — no atomics anywhere", made
  1221  /// expressible.
  1222  ///
  1223  /// Each store keeps its own `pers` field, which is the tier the PARSE and
  1224  /// phase A's setup append to, and ONE flag, `scratch_on`.  **A store is in
  1225  /// one of two states, and "frozen" and "scratch on" are the same thing** (task
  1226  /// #98-FREEZE):
  1227  ///
  1228  /// * **owned, scratch off** (the parse, the setup, between phase A's
  1229  ///   declaration brackets): read through the EMPTY stand-in tier
  1230  ///   (`PersTier::empty`, `frozen` false), so every persistent read and every
  1231  ///   append goes to the owned field;
  1232  /// * **frozen, scratch on** (inside a declaration bracket, and a phase-B
  1233  ///   worker for its whole life): the owned field is empty — `freeze` moved it
  1234  ///   into a `PersTier` whose `frozen` bit is set — and the store is read
  1235  ///   through that tier, so every persistent read goes to it; every append is
  1236  ///   a SCRATCH append, so no append can reach a frozen persistent tier, by
  1237  ///   construction and not by a guard.
  1238  ///
  1239  /// Which tables a persistent read goes to is therefore the READER's to say
  1240  /// (`frozen`), not the store's: the choice is made by a value that is fixed
  1241  /// for the whole of a bracket or a worker, whatever runs inside it.  `freeze`
  1242  /// hands out a frozen tier and turns the scratch tier on; `thaw` takes it back
  1243  /// and turns it off; `empty_frozen` is a worker's store.  Promotion — the one
  1244  /// writer of the persistent tier inside a bracket — writes the frozen tier
  1245  /// itself, through `&mut PersTier` (`PersTier::intern_*`).
  1246  ///
  1247  /// **Why a shared PARAMETER and not a field of the state.**  Task #97-P6-6
  1248  /// measured a region inside the threaded `&mut` state eight ways: a bare
  1249  /// `&u64` field on `AState` costs five function bodies Aeneas cannot
  1250  /// translate and the same borrow inside the four stores costs sixteen, while
  1251  /// everything else this split needs — the two-tier layout, the flag, the
  1252  /// value-returning readers below — extracts at zero errors.  So the sharing
  1253  /// arrives as an ordinary shared parameter, the shape `fe: &IFEnv` and `mode:
  1254  /// &CheckMode` already have, and the twin's monad becomes `ReaderT PersTier
  1255  /// (StateT AState (Except CheckError))`.
  1256  pub struct PersTier {
  1257      /// This is a frozen store's tier: a store read through it reads its
  1258      /// persistent tables HERE.  `false` only for the empty stand-in an owned
  1259      /// store is handed (`PersTier::empty`), which is never read.
  1260      pub frozen: bool,
  1261      pub n: NTables,
  1262      pub l: LTables,
  1263      pub ls: LsTables,
  1264      pub e: ETables,
  1265      /// The stream's index, the frozen base of every job's environment
  1266      /// (`arena::env`'s `IFEnv` note): `checker::freeze_tier` moves it here, so
  1267      /// every worker reads one by reference.  Empty in every other tier.
  1268      pub env: IStreamIndex,
  1269  }

   578  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/FEnv.lean:55-76 FEnv
   579  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Env.lean:232-241 IFEnv` — the environment

   604      /// The base's tables are visible below this record position

   606      pub base_below_rec: u64,

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core_state.rs#L466-L513
   466  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-PERF-WALKMEMO)
   467  /// The slot count past which `take_walk_memo` hands back a FRESH table
   468  /// instead of a cleared one; see its note for how the value was chosen.
   469  pub const WALK_MEMO_KEEP: usize = 1 << 16;
   470  
   471  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/ExprOpsC.lean:2397-2401 allLevelParamsDefinedC
   472  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/StateC.lean:673-675 constsResolveFC
   473  /// Lean twin: the `∅` that `proof/ConRon/Arena/CheckerBase.lean`'s
   474  /// `allLevelParamsDefined` and `constsResolveFFast` start their walk from —
   475  /// **the parked walk memo, moved out of the state and emptied** (task
   476  /// #97-PERF-WALKMEMO).  The slot is left holding `HashMap::new()` (which
   477  /// allocates nothing) for the length of the walk, and the entry puts the
   478  /// grown table back afterwards; either way the table this returns is empty,
   479  /// so the walk starts where the twin's does.
   480  ///
   481  /// **nanoda's guard** (`nanoda_lib/src/expr.rs`, `inst`): a table past
   482  /// `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` slots is dropped rather than kept, so that one huge walk
   483  /// does not leave a huge table behind for every later call.  `reset_map`'s
   484  /// `clear_fit` already decays such a table, one eighth of its high-water mark
   485  /// a call, so the guard only decides which of the two is cheaper for an
   486  /// outlier: re-growing from nothing, or `clear_fit`'s re-make at the decayed
   487  /// size.  The threshold, measured on `Init` (`--verified --jobs=1`, one
   488  /// `perf stat -e instructions:u` run each, all accepting 57 977):
   489  ///
   490  /// | `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` | instructions:u |
   491  /// |---|---:|
   492  /// | fresh `HashMap::new()` per call (before) | 211 976 016 505 |
   493  /// | 2^10 slots (nanoda's 1024) | 208 379 555 799 |
   494  /// | 2^12 | 206 572 063 910 |
   495  /// | 2^14 | 205 851 105 938 |
   496  /// | **2^16** | **205 785 515 243** |
   497  /// | no guard (2^60) | 205 783 023 575 |
   498  ///
   499  /// A guard low enough to trip on ordinary calls gives the saving back — at
   500  /// nanoda's 1024 more than half of it — because those calls re-grow by
   501  /// doubling, which is exactly the cost this table exists to avoid.  2^16 is
   502  /// the smallest power tried that costs nothing measurable on `Init` (2.5 M
   503  /// instructions over no guard), so it only ever fires on an outlier.
   504  pub fn take_walk_memo<K, V>(slot: &mut HashMap<K, V>) -> HashMap<K, V> {
   505      let m: HashMap<K, V> = core::mem::replace(slot, HashMap::new());
   506      if m.capacity() > WALK_MEMO_KEEP {
   507          HashMap::new()
   508      } else {
   509          let mut m2: HashMap<K, V> = m;
   510          reset_map(&mut m2);
   511          m2
   512      }
   513  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/hashmap2.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; a second `Std.HashMap` replacement, proved
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::HashMap2<K, V>` — proved in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean`
     4  //! (task #97-HM2; designed in task #97-P6-4b).  The same abstract object as
     5  //! `ron::hashmap`'s `HashMap` — a partial map from `K` to `V`, with
     6  //! `Hashable`/`Eq2`/`Dup` as its dictionaries and the same eleven operations
     7  //! — over an **open-addressed, epoch-stamped, flat slot vector** instead of
     8  //! the Aeneas tutorial's chained buckets.  `ron::hashmap` is untouched and
     9  //! keeps its proofs (`proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap.lean`); this module's are
    10  //! in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean` (task #97-HM2).
    11  //!
    12  //! **Why it exists.**  Task #97-P6-1 left `clear_slots + allocate_slots +
    13  //! move_elements*` at 21.8 % of `Init`, "all halving recursions over chained
    14  //! buckets".  Task #97-P6-4b counted what those recursions actually do on
    15  //! `Init`, and the counts name the representation rather than the code:
    16  //!
    17  //! | on `Init`, `ron::HashMap` | count |
    18  //! |---|---:|
    19  //! | `get` calls | 1 228 953 968 |
    20  //! | — resolved in 0 or 1 chain step | 98.8 % |
    21  //! | `insert` calls | 627 320 951 |
    22  //! | **`clear` calls** | **36 053 620** |
    23  //! | **— buckets walked by them** | **2 940 488 064** |
    24  //! | — entries those buckets held | 586 917 896 |
    25  //! | buckets pushed by `allocate_slots` | 948 184 512 |
    26  //! | entries moved by `move_elements*` | 349 323 629 |
    27  //!
    28  //! So the chains are *already* short — the table is a good hash table — and
    29  //! essentially all of the 21.8 % is the per-bucket cost of **emptying and
    30  //! re-growing** the slot vector: 2.94 G bucket writes to clear 0.59 G entries
    31  //! (five buckets walked per entry cleared; the average cleared table is 82
    32  //! buckets holding 16 entries) and 0.95 G `Vec::push`es to allocate them back.
    33  //! Nothing a better chain walk can do touches that.
    34  //!
    35  //! **The representation.**
    36  //!
    37  //! * `slots : Vec<Slot<K, V>>`, `Slot` = `Vacant | Live(u32, K, V)`.  No
    38  //!   `Box`, no chain, no allocation per entry — an entry *is* a slot.
    39  //! * A `Live` slot is **live only if its stamp is the table's `epoch`**;
    40  //!   a `Live` slot with a stale stamp is free space, indistinguishable from

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L321-L553
   321  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:224-376 checkMainG
   322  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:87-98 readInputG
   323  /// The driver's front matter: the prelude, the streaming parse, the
   324  /// preparation, the pin walk, the receipts, then the index, the check phase
   325  /// and the verdict.
   326  /// It is the Lean twin's `runPipelineIO` with the heartbeat and the receipts
   327  /// around it (`Arena/Main.lean`), and `con-ron`'s `check_main` with the
   328  /// handles in place of the trees.
   329  fn check_main(a: &Args, input: &Input) -> u8 {
   330      let t0 = Instant::now();
   331      let mode_tag = if a.verified {
   332          "--verified"
   333      } else {
   334          "--trusted"
   335      };
   336      let mode = if a.verified {
   337          CheckMode::Verified
   338      } else {
   339          CheckMode::Trusted
   340      };
   341      // ONE store for the whole run: the prelude, the stream and the pins are
   342      // hash-consed together into its persistent tier (DESIGN.md §8.3).
   343      // ConRon.Capstone: `startState`
   344      let mut st = AState::empty();
   345      // THE PERSISTENT TIER a worker reads (DESIGN.md §8.3, task #97-P6-6b).
   346      // The parse, the pin walk and the index build own their own — the store is
   347      // owned (not frozen) — so what they are handed here is the EMPTY tier; the
   348      // check phase freezes the store's tier, the index with it, into a
   349      // `PersTier` and hands `&` it to every worker (`check_decls_driver`).
   350      // ConRon.Capstone: `emptyTier`
   351      let pers: &PersTier = &PersTier::empty();
   352      // THE RESERVED-NAME PINS, interned once into that persistent tier before
   353      // anything else touches it (task #97-P6-4a, `arena::pins`): the scratch
   354      // tier is closed here, so every pinned handle is persistent and survives
   355      // every job's bracket.  Until this has run, every `pin_*`
   356      // read raises `Internal` rather than answering — which is what makes the
   357      // initialisation-order hazard task #97c named impossible rather than
   358      // unlikely.
   359      // ConRon.Capstone: h1
   360      match con_ron_core::arena::pins::intern_reserved_pins(pers, &mut st) {
   361          Ok(()) => (),
   362          Err(e) => {
   363              eprintln!(
   364                  "con-ron: the reserved-name pins do not intern ({}) ({})",
   365                  con_ron::driver::message(&e),
   366                  mode_tag
   367              );
   368              return 3;
   369          }
   370      }
   371      // The heartbeat (`--progress`), and its first line: what the run reads.
   372      let mut hb = Heartbeat::new(con_ron_core::frontend::pace::pace_dup(&a.progress), t0);
   373      hb.read_starts(&match input {
   374          Input::Ndjson(file) => con_ron::render::display_path(file),
   375          Input::Oleans(req) => req.label(pers, &st),
   376      });
   377      // THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE, parsed into that store before anything else.
   378      // ConRon.Capstone: h2
   379      let prelude_ix = match prelude::builtin_prelude_e(pers, &mut st) {
   380          Ok(p) => p,
   381          Err((e, line)) => {
   382              let what = match classify(&e) {
   383                  FrontendClass::Internal(m) => format!("does not parse (line {}: {})", line, m),
   384                  FrontendClass::Declined(w) => format!("is unsupported ({})", w),
   385                  FrontendClass::Invalid(w) => format!("contradicts itself ({})", w),
   386              };
   387              eprintln!(
   388                  "con-ron: the built-in prelude {}; regenerate it with \
   389                   `lake exe natop-pins-export` ({})",
   390                  what, mode_tag
   391              );
   392              return 3;
   393          }
   394      };
   395      // Streaming frontend: the file is read 4 MiB at a time and each buffer is
   396      // parsed and dropped, so neither a wholesale text buffer nor a scratch
   397      // file exists.  What comes out is the FILE's records as HANDLES into the
   398      // store above.  No model is ever read from the input: every inductive
   399      // block — mutual and nested included — installs through the kernel's
   400      // uniform installer, unconditionally (task #105).
   401      // ConRon.Capstone: hreads, h3 (`parse_source` over the file's handle)
   402      // The `.olean` path ends in the same records (task #142); no capstone
   403      // premise is about it yet (OVERVIEW.md).
   404      // An `--olean` run's theorems hold references to their values, which their
   405      // jobs read (`driver::olean_job`); what that needs comes back beside the
   406      // records (`OleanRead`), and of it the check keeps only the pins and the
   407      // values (below, after the preparation).
   408      let read: std::io::Result<Result<(Vec<IDeclaration>, Option<OleanRead>), (CheckError, u64)>> = match input {
   409          Input::Ndjson(file) => match driver::parse_export_stream_d(pers, &mut st, file, export_c::CHUNK_SIZE) {
   410              Err(e) => {
   411                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}: {}", con_ron::render::display_path(file), e);
   412                  return 3;
   413              }
   414              Ok((r, _)) => Ok(r.map(|p: ParseResultD| (p.decls, None))),
   415          },
   416          Input::Oleans(req) => Ok(con_ron::olean_fs::read_request(pers, &mut st, req, &a.progress)
   417              .map(|mut rd| (std::mem::take(&mut rd.decls), Some(rd)))),
   418      };
   419      let label: String = match input {
   420          Input::Ndjson(file) => con_ron::render::display_path(file),
   421          Input::Oleans(req) => req.label(pers, &st),
   422      };
   423      let (parsed_decls, olean): (Vec<IDeclaration>, Option<OleanRead>) = match read {
   424          Err(_) => return 3,
   425          Ok(Err((e, line))) => match classify(&e) {
   426              FrontendClass::Declined(what) => {
   427                  eprintln!("con-ron: declined: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   428                  return 2;
   429              }
   430              // A stream whose inductive block contradicts its own declarations
   431              // in a REDUNDANT field is rejected at the parse.
   432              FrontendClass::Invalid(what) => {
   433                  eprintln!("con-ron: invalid: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   434                  return 1;
   435              }
   436              FrontendClass::Internal(msg) => {
   437                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}:{}: {}", label, line, msg);
   438                  return 3;
   439              }
   440          },
   441          Ok(Ok(r)) => r,
   442      };
   443      let file_records = parsed_decls.len();
   444      // From here on the store is the checker's state: the memo tables and the
   445      // per-declaration caches join it (`AState`), and every handle the parse
   446      // produced indexes into it.
   447      // **PREPARE** (`frontend::prepare`): what the fold runs over is
   448      // `prepare_prelude` of the file's records — the prelude's declarations
   449      // first (the stream's own copies where it has them, the rest synthesised),
   450      // then the stream's, with every pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
   451      // ground hoisted ahead of it.  It takes the whole state since task
   452      // #97-P4d: step 2 is the real ground hoist, which interns.
   453      // ConRon.Capstone: h4
   454      // What a record mentions, for the ground hoist: its expressions say it,
   455      // except a theorem's read from an `.olean`, whose load read it off the
   456      // file (con-leche's `usedOf`).
   457      let prepared = match match &olean {
   458          None => prepare::prepare_d(pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed_decls, &DeclUsedConsts),
   459          Some(rd) => prepare::prepare_d(pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed_decls, rd),
   460      } {
   461          Ok(p) => p,
   462          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   463      };
   464      // **What the check keeps of the read** (con-leche's `checkOleansG` takes
   465      // `rd.values`): the reader's pins and the values' modules.  The merged
   466      // constants, whose last reader is the preparation (`OleanRead.thmUses`), go
   467      // here, before the pool: on Mathlib that is 0.8 M constants and their
   468      // `uses` (DESIGN, task #145).
   469      let olean: Option<(OleanPins, Vec<ModRef>)> =
   470          olean.map(|rd| (rd.pins, rd.values));
   471      // the ground hoist's receipt
   472      if !prepared.hoisted.is_empty() {
   473          let names: Vec<String> = prepared
   474              .hoisted
   475              .iter()
   476              .map(|n| driver::name_of(pers, &st.store, n))
   477              .collect();
   478          eprintln!(
   479              "con-ron: {} declarations hoisted ahead of the pinned Nat operations \
   480               they ground: {}",
   481              prepared.hoisted.len(),
   482              names.join(", ")
   483          );
   484      }
   485      // ConRon.Capstone: hpins (`decode_embedded`; `--pins`/`--no-pins` are
   486      // outside the theorems)
   487      let pins = match con_ron::driver::pins_for_run(&a.pins, a.no_pins) {
   488          Ok(p) => p,
   489          Err(e) => {
   490              eprintln!("con-ron: {}", e);
   491              return 3;
   492          }
   493      };
   494      // What the parse line reports, printed once the index is built.
   495      hb.file_records = file_records;
   496      hb.synthesised = prepared.synthesised;
   497      // **THE STARTUP PIN WALK** (DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d, task #97-P4d): every
   498      // pinned datum the checker compares a stream record against — the six
   499      // basis blocks in both forms, the axiom pins, the reserved names and the
   500      // `Nat`-operation variants — interned ONCE, here, while the scratch tier
   501      // is still off, so that nothing the fold compares against lives in a tier
   502      // that is about to vanish.  Its result is the fold's pin parameter.
   503      // ConRon.Capstone: h5
   504      let ipins = match checker::intern_all_pins(pers, &mut st, &pins, &a.max_nat_size) {
   505          Ok(p) => p,
   506          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   507      };
   508      // ONE driver, and the heartbeat is printed between its steps
   509      // (`driver::check_decls_driver`: the index, the frozen tier, and the pool
   510      // for the check phase).
   511      let jobs: u64 = match a.jobs {
   512          Some(n) => n,
   513          None => con_ron::driver::default_jobs(),
   514      };
   515      // ONE lane, whatever the flags: the driver is what builds and freezes the
   516      // index and the check phase is the pool at every worker count, so a run
   517      // with no heartbeat is the same computation as a run with one.
   518      // ConRon.Capstone: the index, the freeze and the pool (the driver's steps,
   519      // either observer)
   520      let on = con_ron_core::frontend::pace::pace_on(&a.progress);
   521      let ds = &prepared.decls;
   522      let verdict = match (&olean, input) {
   523          (Some((pk, values)), Input::Oleans(req)) => {
   524              let sp = &req.search_path;
   525              let job = |tier: &PersTier, w: &mut AState, c: &mut ValueCache, k: u64| {
   526                  driver::olean_job(tier, w, c, &mode, &ipins, ds, pk, values, sp, k)
   527              };
   528              if on {
   529                  driver::check_decls_driver_with(pers, &mut st, ds, jobs, &mut hb, value_cache_empty, job)
   530              } else {
   531                  driver::check_decls_driver_with(pers, &mut st, ds, jobs, &mut driver::Silent, value_cache_empty, job)
   532              }
   533          }
   534          _ => {
   535              if on {
   536                  driver::check_decls_driver(pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, ds, jobs, &mut hb)
   537              } else {
   538                  driver::check_decls_driver(pers, &mut st, &mode, &ipins, ds, jobs, &mut driver::Silent)
   539              }
   540          }
   541      };
   542      // **The headline number is the FILE's declaration-record count**: the
   543      // records the PARSE produced, which are the file's own.  Nothing the
   544      // preparation does moves it.
   545      let stream_records = file_records as u64;
   546      let code = match &verdict {
   547          Ok(_) => driver::verdict_accept(stream_records, mode_tag),
   548          Err((e, i)) => {
   549              driver::verdict_failure(pers, &st.store, &prepared.decls, e, *i, mode_tag, t0)
   550          }
   551      };
   552      exit_after_verdict(code)
   553  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/pins.rs#L1-L60
     1  //! `arena::pins` — the reserved names, interned ONCE (task #97-P6-4a).
     2  //!
     3  //! con-leche compares its reserved names — `natName`, `natZeroName`,
     4  //! `natSuccName`, the sixteen `Nat`-operation names, the `Bool` trio, the
     5  //! `String`/`List`/`Char` family, the standard and the trusted axiom names —
     6  //! as `Name` VALUES, which Lean builds once per nullary `def` and caches.
     7  //! The arena compares them as HANDLES, so `arena::core::pin` turned each one
     8  //! into `intern_name` of a freshly built `Name`: a `code_points` allocation
     9  //! and an `Arc<NameNode>` per path segment, then one cons-table probe per
    10  //! segment, every time.  Task #97-P6-1's counter measured what that costs on
    11  //! `Init`: **140 083 646 `NStore::intern` calls, of which 88 854 033 are
    12  //! probes of a `str` node built purely to be compared and dropped** — tens of
    13  //! millions of rebuilds of about forty constants, in `natLitSupported`'s
    14  //! three probes per literal, in `natOpNames`, in `strLitToConstructor`.
    15  //!
    16  //! This module is DESIGN.md's answer, flagged at task #97c ("the `Pins`
    17  //! record that is NOT here") and deferred there for want of a number: one
    18  //! record, filled once at the driver by `intern_reserved_pins`, and every
    19  //! `pin` of a constant name becomes a field read.
    20  //!
    21  //! **Not `arena::checker`'s `intern_all_pins`.**  That one walks the `--pins`
    22  //! RECEIPT file (the trusted pin list) into the persistent tier; this one
    23  //! interns the checker's own reserved constants.  The two run at the same
    24  //! point of the pipeline and mean different things, which is why they have
    25  //! different names.
    26  //!
    27  //! ## The table is a `Vec`, and that is what kills task #97c's hazard
    28  //!
    29  //! Task #97c declined the record because of an initialisation-order hazard:
    30  //! "a pin read before it is filled compares against the zero word and
    31  //! silently says *not `Nat`*".  A record of handle FIELDS has that hazard,
    32  //! because every 32-bit word is a syntactically valid handle.  A `Vec<NIdx>`
    33  //! does not: before `intern_reserved_pins` runs the table is EMPTY, so `pin_at`
    34  //! takes its bounds branch and raises `CheckError::Internal` — a loud stop,
    35  //! never a quiet wrong answer.  The cost is one `len` compare per read,
    36  //! against an interning walk it replaces.
    37  //!
    38  //! ## What is pinned
    39  //!
    40  //! The fifty-two names below and `basis_names::reserved_basis_names()`'s
    41  //! sixteen, plus the three interned values every `pin` site around them
    42  //! needs: the empty universe-argument list, the level `0` and the expression
    43  //! `Sort 1` (`arena::core`'s `empty_levels`, `zero_level` and `sort_one`,
    44  //! which now read this record instead of interning).
    45  //!
    46  //! All of them go into the PERSISTENT tier, because `intern_reserved_pins` runs
    47  //! before the parse, while the scratch tier is closed.  That matters twice:
    48  //! a pinned handle must survive every `drop_scratch` (it is read across all
    49  //! of them), and task #97-P6-1's `pers_find_maybe` rests on "a persistent
    50  //! node's children are persistent", which the bottom-up intern of a closed
    51  //! scratch tier gives for free.
    52  //!
    53  //! **Denotation unchanged.**  A pin is `intern_name` of the same `Name`, so
    54  //! the handle this record holds is the handle `pin` computed before —
    55  //! `denoteN` is injective and `intern` is idempotent, so pre-interning a name
    56  //! the export also carries hands the export's parse the very same handle.
    57  //! What changes is only WHEN the intern happens, and how many times.
    58  //!
    59  //! Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:118-135 AState` (DESIGN.md §8.6's
    60  //! twin ledger, task #97-P6-4a) — `AState` gains a `pins : Pins` field and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/prepare.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Prepare.lean` — **what happens between the
     2  //! file and the fold** (task #97 P4e part 1).
     3  //!
     4  //! `prepare_prelude` is total — no record of the stream is dropped, rewritten
     5  //! or retagged — and it does two things:
     6  //!
     7  //! 1. **the prelude's declarations first**, the stream's OWN copy of each
     8  //!    where the stream has one and a synthesised one only where it has none,
     9  //!    so a stream that declares the toolchain's `Bool` is checked on its own
    10  //!    `Bool` record;
    11  //! 2. **the ground hoist**: a pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
    12  //!    structural ground is moved ahead of it when the stream declares it
    13  //!    later.
    14  //!
    15  //! Moving a record earlier can only reject, never accept, which is why the
    16  //! spec con-leche proves is as simple as it is:
    17  //!
    18  //! ```text
    19  //! ∃ extra, (∀ d ∈ extra, d ∈ prelude) ∧
    20  //!   (preparePrelude ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra)
    21  //! ```
    22  //!
    23  //! **Step 2 is `frontend::nat_op_ground`'s**, a module of its own exactly as
    24  //! con-leche's is (task #97-P4d; task #97-P4e part 1 shipped an identity
    25  //! placeholder here, because the pass needs the kernel's
    26  //! `natOpNames`/`natDivModNames`, which arrived with the pins).  It is why
    27  //! `prepare_d` takes the whole `AState` where everything else in this module
    28  //! needs only the store.
    29  //!
    30  //! **Where the store comes from.**  Only `prelude_key`, whose `.anonymous`
    31  //! fall-through has to be INTERNED, and the two functions that call it;
    32  //! [`pick_idx`] and [`declares`] are pure, exactly as con-leche's are, because
    33  //! `env::i_declaration_names` is.
    34  //! Nothing in this module reads or writes a term.
    35  //!
    36  //! **The deviation of the port into the verified core** (task #84), kept
    37  //! verbatim from `con_ron_core::frontend::prepare`: con-leche's `pick` ERASES
    38  //! the picked record from the array (`Array.eraseIdxIfInBounds`) and `frontOf`
    39  //! moves it to the front.  The Aeneas subset has no operation that takes an
    40  //! element out of a `Vec` — no `remove`, no `pop`, no `into_iter` — so the
    41  //! port splits the two halves that con-leche fuses: [`pick_idx`] is the cited
    42  //! `ds.findIdx (declares n)` with the erasure recorded in a `picked` mask
    43  //! instead of performed, [`front_of`] runs that over the prelude, and
    44  //! [`prepared_stream`] materialises the whole prepared list in ONE pass.  The
    45  //! list that comes out is the same list; the cost is one record copy per
    46  //! record, where the copied fields are handles and `Vec` spines and not terms.
    47  //! con-leche's `pickSpec`/`frontSpec` are not ported (they are `cons`-list
    48  //! specifications with no caller on the run path); `pick_spec` lives in this
    49  //! module's tests, where it still checks `pick_idx` against the specification
    50  //! on every `cargo test`.

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L164-L199
   164  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/NatOpPins.lean:75-78 _
   165  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Basis.lean:39-45 BasisKind.decls
   166  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:124-162 internAllPins` — **the
   167  /// one-time tree walk of DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d**: every datum the checker compares
   168  /// a stream record against, interned into the tier that is live at the call —
   169  /// which, at the driver's call, is the persistent one.
   170  ///
   171  /// The five basis blocks' pins (what a basis block's and a quotient record's
   172  /// job compares the record with), the standard and compiler-trust axiom pins, the reserved names
   173  /// the guards compare by handle, and the `Nat`-operation pin variants, whose
   174  /// interned form is the checker's pin-list parameter (con-leche's task #304).
   175  /// First, the run's maximum `Nat` size goes into the pin record
   176  /// (`Pins::max_nat_size`): con-leche threads it beside the pin list
   177  /// (`checkDecls mode pins maxNatSize`) into every declaration's fresh state
   178  /// (`{ maxNatSize := maxNatSize }`, `Cached.declStep`, `Cached.recordJob`); here
   179  /// every worker copies it with the pins (`worker_state`) and no job writes it.
   180  /// It is stored normalised (`nat::norm`), whatever limbs the caller hands in,
   181  /// so every comparison against it reads it as the number it denotes.
   182  pub fn intern_all_pins(
   183      pers: &PersTier,
   184      st: &mut AState,
   185      pins: &Vec<NatOpPinSet>,
   186      max_nat_size: &Nat,
   187  ) -> Result<Vec<INatOpPinSet>, CheckError> {
   188      st.pins.max_nat_size = nat::norm(nat::clone(max_nat_size).limbs);
   189      match intern_all_basis(pers, st, 0) {
   190          Err(e) => Err(e),
   191          Ok(()) => match intern_all_axiom_pins(pers, st) {
   192              Err(e) => Err(e),
   193              Ok(()) => match intern_all_names(st) {
   194                  Err(e) => Err(e),
   195                  Ok(()) => intern_pin_sets(pers, st, pins, 0, Vec::new()),
   196              },
   197          },
   198      }
   199  }

  1341          Err(bad_text())
  1342      } else {
  1343          run_records(t, hdr.len(), tables_new())
  1344      }
  1345  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/mod.rs#L19-L30
    19  //! | Rust | Lean twin | con-leche |
    20  //! |---|---|---|
    21  //! | `text` | none | none — the port's message rendering (`String` is `Vec<u32>`) |
    22  //! | `nat_decimal` | none | none — `String.toNat?` on a `natVal` literal (`ron::nat` has no decimal codec) |
    23  //! | `scan_types` | imported, not twinned | `ConLeche/Frontend/Scan/Types.lean` |
    24  //! | `scan_fast` | imported, not twinned | `ConLeche/Frontend/Scan/Fast.lean` (the `@[csimp]` twin the compiler *runs*; `Scan/Naive.lean` is the specification and is not ported) |
    25  //! | `prelude_text` | `include_str` | `ConLeche/Frontend/Prelude.lean:57-62`'s `include_str` — **generated**, `scripts/gen-prelude.sh` |
    26  //! | `types` | `Arena/Frontend/Types.lean` | `Frontend/Export.lean`'s verdicts |
    27  //! | `export_c` | `Arena/Frontend/ExportC.lean` | `Frontend/ExportC.lean` |

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L950-L991
   950  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:188-198 foldChunks
   951  /// **The file handle as the parse's `ChunkSource`**: each `next_chunk` is one
   952  /// `read_up_to` of `chunk` bytes, strictly forward, handed over whole; the
   953  /// first empty read is the end of the input.  A failed read ends the input
   954  /// the same way and is KEPT here, and `parse_export_handle_d` reports it in
   955  /// place of whatever the parse of the truncated input said — so a read error
   956  /// is exit 3, never a verdict, as before the loop moved.
   957  pub struct HandleSource<'a, R: Read> {
   958      /// The open reader.
   959      pub h: &'a mut R,
   960      /// The buffer size, `export_c::CHUNK_SIZE` in the binary.
   961      pub chunk: usize,
   962      /// The nonempty buffers handed out so far, for the heartbeat.
   963      pub chunks: u64,
   964      /// The first read failure, if any.
   965      pub err: Option<std::io::Error>,
   966  }
   967  
   968  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:188-198 foldChunks
   969  impl<'a, R: Read> ChunkSource for HandleSource<'a, R> {
   970      /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:188-198 foldChunks
   971      /// One read of up to `chunk` bytes; empty at the end or on a failure.
   972      fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
   973          if self.err.is_some() {
   974              return Vec::new();
   975          }
   976          let mut buf: Vec<u8> = vec![0u8; self.chunk];
   977          match read_up_to(self.h, &mut buf) {
   978              Ok(n) => {
   979                  buf.truncate(n);
   980                  if n > 0 {
   981                      self.chunks += 1;
   982                  }
   983                  buf
   984              }
   985              Err(e) => {
   986                  self.err = Some(e);
   987                  Vec::new()
   988              }
   989          }
   990      }
   991  }

   170      ix: IStreamIndex,

   176      } else {

   181      }
   182  }

   632  pub fn olean_job(
   633      tier: &PersTier,
   634      w: &mut AState,
   635      cache: &mut con_ron_core::frontend::olean::records::ValueCache,
   636      mode: &CheckMode,
   637      pins: &Vec<INatOpPinSet>,
   638      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   639      pk: &con_ron_core::frontend::olean::spec::OleanPins,
   640      values: &Vec<con_ron_core::frontend::olean::records::ModRef>,
   641      sp: &Vec<Vec<u32>>,

   643  ) -> Result<(), (CheckError, u64)> {

   645          Some(d) => d,
   646          None => return checker::run_job(tier, w, mode, pins, ds, k),
   647      };
   648      let code: Option<u64> = match d {
   649          // a theorem's value is a reference only if its handle is a `bvar`: the store's
   650          // projection reads the bvar table at the handle's slot whatever its tag
   651          IDeclaration::ThmDecl(_, v) if v.tag() == con_ron_core::arena::handle::ETAG_BVAR => {
   652              w.store.view_bvar(tier, v)
   653          }
   654          _ => None,
   655      };
   656      match (code, d) {

   666                  cache,
   667                  code,
   668              ) {
   669                  Err(e) => Err((e, k)),
   670                  Ok(v) => {
   671                      let pd = IDeclaration::ThmDecl(ienv::i_constant_val_dup(cv), v);
   672                      match stream_index::record_check(tier, w, mode, pins, k, &pd) {
   673                          Err(e) => Err((e, k)),
   674                          Ok(()) => Ok(()),
   675                      }
   676                  }
   677              };
   678              con_ron_core::arena::core::leave_record(w);
   679              r
   680          }
   681          _ => checker::run_job(tier, w, mode, pins, ds, k),
   682      }

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L559-L619
   559  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:224-376 checkMainG
   560  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:152-169 checkOleansG
   561  /// `check_decls_driver` with a worker state of the caller's beside each
   562  /// worker's `AState` (`init_x`, one per worker) and the caller's job: an
   563  /// `--olean` run's workers keep the module region they read a theorem's value
   564  /// from (`olean_job`, con-leche's `OleanWorker`), every other run's job is
   565  /// `checker::run_job` with nothing beside it.
   566  pub fn check_decls_driver_with<O, X, I, J>(
   567      pers: &PersTier,
   568      st: &mut AState,
   569      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   570      jobs: u64,
   571      obs: &mut O,
   572      init_x: I,
   573      job: J,
   574  ) -> Result<(), (CheckError, u64)>
   575  where
   576      O: PhaseObserver + Send,
   577      I: Fn() -> X + Sync,
   578      J: Fn(&PersTier, &mut AState, &mut X, u64) -> Result<(), (CheckError, u64)> + Sync,
   579  {
   580      // THE INDEX (the last step of the parse phase): every record's constants and
   581      // tables, a name's first entry winning, read off the records alone.
   582      obs.index_starts();
   583      let ix: IStreamIndex = stream_index::build_index(pers, st, stream_index::stream_index_empty(), ds, 0)?;
   584      obs.parse_done(pers, &st.store, ds.len());
   585      let m = ds.len();
   586      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   587      obs.check_starts(m, workers);
   588      // THE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier and the index leave the state and become
   589      // a value every worker reads.  `st` keeps its (empty) store, its tables
   590      // moved out, so the observer can still read a label back through the tier.
   591      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store, ix);
   592      // THE CHECK PHASE: the job at every record, on `workers` threads, each
   593      // folding it over the jobs it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the verdict and
   594      // the record a rejection names are the one-worker walk's at every `--jobs`.
   595      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   596      let lock: Mutex<(usize, &mut O)> = Mutex::new((0, obs));
   597      let r = parallel_all(
   598          m,
   599          workers,
   600          || (checker::worker_state(&st.pins), init_x()),
   601          |w: &mut (AState, X), k| job(&tier, &mut w.0, &mut w.1, k as u64),
   602          |w: &(AState, X), k| check_line(heartbeat, &lock, &tier, &w.0, m, ds, k),
   603      );
   604      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   605          Ok((_, o)) => o,
   606          Err(e) => e.into_inner().1,
   607      };
   608      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the check — the verdict line's
   609      // declaration label, the failing record's name — reads a handle back out of
   610      // `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has gone out of scope
   611      // answers `None` to every one of them.
   612      let _ix: IStreamIndex = checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   613      let v = pool_verdict(r);
   614      obs.check_done(m, match &v {
   615          Err((_, pos)) => Some(*pos),
   616          Ok(()) => None,
   617      });
   618      v
   619  }

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L35-L48
    35  //! ## What a worker is, in the check phase
    36  //!
    37  //! §8.3 has said since P1 what the check phase is: "the persistent tier is
    38  //! immutable, each worker owns a scratch tier — **no atomics anywhere**"
    39  //! (`record_job` is the bracket; nothing writes the persistent tier after the
    40  //! index is built and frozen, and a worker never holds it `&mut`).  So the
    41  //! driver's `init`
    42  //! builds `checker::worker_state(pins)` — an EMPTY store, FROZEN
    43  //! (`EStore::empty_frozen`: every append a scratch append), its own `Memos`
    44  //! and `Caches`, and a COPY of
    45  //! the driver's `Pins` — and its `step` borrows the frozen `&PersTier`, which
    46  //! holds the stream's index.  A job reads it through an empty layer of its own
    47  //! at its record's view and pushes into that layer.  So a worker costs no
    48  //! environment copy at all.

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L121-L135
   121  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:199-227 checkPool
   122  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:64-71 AState.worker` — the twin's
   123  /// worker reads the persistent tier where it is.
   124  /// **A worker's start state** (the cited `init`): the empty store, FROZEN
   125  /// (`EStore::empty_frozen`, task #98-FREEZE), so that every persistent read goes
   126  /// to the `PersTier` the boundary froze and every append is a scratch append;
   127  /// fresh memos and caches; and a copy of the pins, the run's maximum `Nat` size
   128  /// among them (con-leche's `checkPool mode maxNatSize`, which hands it to every
   129  /// job's fresh state through `runAt` and `recordJob`).  The store stays frozen for
   130  /// the worker's life: `record_job` only empties its scratch tier.
   131  pub fn worker_state(pins: &Pins) -> AState {
   132      let mut st = AState::init(EStore::empty_frozen());
   133      st.pins = pins_dup(pins);
   134      st
   135  }

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L232-L293
   232  
   233  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:457-483 parMapWorkersIO
   234  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:199-227 checkPool
   235  /// **`step` at every index of `0..n`, on a pool of `workers` threads** — the
   236  /// module note's trusted claim is this function's contract:
   237  ///
   238  /// > If it returns `Ok(())`, every index in `0..n` was claimed by some worker,
   239  /// > each worker built its state with `init()` once and folded `step` over its
   240  /// > claimed indices in claim order, which is increasing, and every step
   241  /// > returned `Ok(())`.
   242  ///
   243  /// On a failure it returns the LEAST failing index with its error
   244  /// (`ParallelError::Step`), whatever the timing.  `after(&st, k)` runs on the
   245  /// worker's thread after each step it made, with the worker's state by `&`
   246  /// (the driver's heartbeat); it cannot change an outcome.
   247  ///
   248  /// The workers are `std::thread::scope`d, with `STACK_BYTES` of stack each.
   249  /// `workers` is the count the caller has already clamped
   250  /// (`driver::workers_for`: `max(1, min(jobs, n))`); if the OS refuses to
   251  /// spawn one, the pool runs on those it has, and on the calling thread if it
   252  /// has none — the contract holds at every worker count, so the answer does
   253  /// not depend on it.
   254  pub fn parallel_all<S, E: Send>(
   255      n: usize,
   256      workers: usize,
   257      init: impl Fn() -> S + Sync,
   258      step: impl Fn(&mut S, usize) -> Result<(), E> + Sync,
   259      after: impl Fn(&S, usize) + Sync,
   260  ) -> Result<(), ParallelError<E>> {
   261      let next = AtomicUsize::new(0);
   262      let limit = AtomicUsize::new(n);
   263      let run = || worker(n, &next, &limit, &init, &step, &after);
   264      let mut results: Vec<Vec<(usize, Result<(), E>)>> = Vec::with_capacity(workers);
   265      let mut panicked = false;
   266      std::thread::scope(|scope| {
   267          let mut handles = Vec::with_capacity(workers);
   268          for w in 0..workers {
   269              let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
   270                  .stack_size(STACK_BYTES)
   271                  .name(format!("check-{}", w))
   272                  .spawn_scoped(scope, &run);
   273              match spawned {
   274                  Ok(h) => handles.push(h),
   275                  // Out of threads, or out of address space for another stack:
   276                  // run on the workers already spawned (the module note).
   277                  Err(_) => break,
   278              }
   279          }
   280          if handles.is_empty() {
   281              results.push(run());
   282          }
   283          for h in handles {
   284              match h.join() {
   285                  Ok(rs) => results.push(rs),
   286                  Err(_) => panicked = true,
   287              }
   288          }
   289      });
   290      if panicked {
   291          return Err(ParallelError::Panicked);
   292      }
   293      first_failure(merge_results(n, results))

== proof/ConRon/Arena/Denote.lean#L185-L208
   185  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:341-460 Expr — the fuel-indexed
   186  readback of an expression handle. -/
   187  def denoteEAux (st : EStore) : Nat → EIdx → Option Expr
   188    | 0, _ => none
   189    | f + 1, i =>
   190      (st.view i).bind fun v =>
   191        match v with
   192        | .bvar k => some (.bvar k)
   193        | .fvar k ty => (denoteEAux st f ty).map (Expr.fvar k)
   194        | .sort u => (denoteL st.ls u).map Expr.sort
   195        | .const n us => opt2 Expr.const (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteLs st.lss us)
   196        | .app g a => opt2 Expr.app (denoteEAux st f g) (denoteEAux st f a)
   197        | .lam ty b => opt2 Expr.lam (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   198        | .forallE ty b => opt2 Expr.forallE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   199        | .letE ty w b =>
   200          opt3 Expr.letE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f w) (denoteEAux st f b)
   201        | .lit l => some (.lit l)
   202        | .proj n k e =>
   203          opt2 (fun nm x => Expr.proj nm k x) (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteEAux st f e)
   204  
   205  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:341-460 Expr — the readback of an
   206  expression handle, at the store's own node count as fuel. -/
   207  def denoteE (st : EStore) (i : EIdx) : Option Expr :=
   208    denoteEAux st (st.nodeCount + 1) i

== proof/ConRon/Arena/WF.lean#L1-L39
     1  /-
     2  # Store well-formedness and the store layer's theorems (DESIGN.md §8.3, P2a)
     3  
     4  `StoreWF` is the arena's own invariant — con-leche's `TWF`
     5  (`Setlec/Kernel/ArenaWF.lean:900`, 28 clauses) redrawn for the
     6  per-constructor, high-tag representation.  It lives here, beside the
     7  implementation, importing nothing from `ConRon.Refine`: con-leche's lesson 27,
     8  "implementation may import a *self-contained* data-structure verification".
     9  
    10  Each store's invariant is `∃ rank, …WFAt st rank`.  The rank is existential
    11  because nothing at runtime stores it (DESIGN §8.3: "zero runtime cost, and no
    12  global array order is needed with per-constructor arrays"); what it buys is
    13  
    14  * **acyclicity**, hence a terminating `denote`;
    15  * **a fuel bound**: a persistent node's rank is below the persistent node
    16    count and a scratch node's below the total, so `nodeCount + 1` — the fuel
    17    `denoteE` uses — is always enough, and `dropScratch` shrinks both sides of
    18    the persistent clause together.
    19  
    20  The clauses, in the order a reader meets them:
    21  
    22  | clause | what it says |
    23  |---|---|
    24  | `childOK` | every child is in range, ranked below its parent, and persistent if the parent is |
    25  | `rankP` / `rankS` | ranks are below the tier's node count (the fuel bound) |
    26  | `consP` / `consS` | each tier's cons table is exactly the inverse of that tier's `get` |
    27  | `fresh` | a scratch cons entry never duplicates a persistent one (DESIGN §8.3's cross-tier canonicity; con-leche's `t_cons_fresh`) |
    28  | `derExact` | the derived column is `derOfView` of the node — *locally*; the global `derived st i = e.data` is a theorem (`derived_exact`) |
    29  | `sized` | the derived array is as long as the node array |
    30  | `cap` | no constructor array exceeds its handle shape's index range (2^30 for `app`, 2^26 for the rest), so the index is injective on it |
    31  | `scrOff` | the scratch tier is empty while the scratch flag is off |
    32  | `sync` | the nesting's scratch flags move together (task #97a) |
    33  
    34  `childOK`'s third conjunct — *persistent parents have persistent children* —
    35  is what makes `dropScratch` sound: without it a persistent node could point
    36  into a tier that is about to vanish.  It needs no hypothesis at `intern`,
    37  because `scrOff` makes a scratch handle undecodable while the flag is off, so
    38  a valid child of a node appended to the persistent tier is persistent already.
    39  -/

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Specs.lean#L1-L31
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Bridge.Specs` — one `@[spec]` theorem per `Monad.lean` primitive
     3  
     4  **One spec theorem per (B) primitive, in one shape**, so that the
     5  verification-condition generator (`vcgen`, on native `Std.WP` triples) can
     6  walk a twin's body without any store reasoning appearing in the proof text.
     7  The shape is the seven-rule template (DESIGN §8.6, `P2s SPIKE`, and task
     8  #97s's section):
     9  
    10  ```lean
    11  @[spec] theorem f_spec (s₀ : AState) (args…) (pre…) :
    12      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ f args ⦃fun r s' => Post s₀ r s'; ⊤⦄
    13  ```
    14  
    15  1. **the precondition is `s = s₀` and nothing else** — every real
    16     precondition is an ordinary hypothesis of the theorem, so `vcgen` turns it
    17     into a side goal instead of an entailment to discharge in the logic;
    18  2. **exception postcondition `⊤` (partial correctness), never the default
    19     `⊥`** (`⦃P⦄ x ⦃Q⦄` is TOTAL correctness in `Std.WP`) — a (B) function may
    20     fail and Theorem 1 claims nothing then (con-leche's `SimAt`,
    21     `Verify/SimI.lean:244`);
    22  3. **the postcondition names `s₀`**, the only way to state
    23     `Ext s₀.store s'.store` in a triple;
    24  4. **"the subject denotes" is an `isSome`, never a named `Expr`**;
    25  5. **the answer is a named relation or predicate** (`Rel.lean`'s `RelE`
    26     family, `Grind.lean`'s `Ans`/`MapRel`), never a bare `∀ e, … → …`;
    27  6. **a memo insert's spec states that the INVARIANT is preserved**, not that
    28     the table grew — the rule that matters most;
    29  7. **one named failure primitive** (`fail`): every failure site goes
    30     through it, so one spec covers them all and the Rust has one function to
    31     match.

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Run.lean#L60-L76
    60  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/SimI.lean:244 SimAt — **the PURE grade's
    61  statement**: from a well-formed store, an ACCEPTING run of the twin returns an
    62  answer related to the pure side's by `R`, having only grown the arena.
    63  
    64  Partial correctness, as everywhere in this library: a (B) function may fail
    65  and Theorem 1 claims nothing then — which is why the hypothesis is
    66  `c s0 = .ok (r, s')` and not an unconditional equation.
    67  
    68  **RUN form rather than a Hoare triple** (DESIGN `### Task #97-P3-Checker`
    69  §1): this tier's work is composition, inversion and list induction rather
    70  than verification conditions, and the checker tier that consumes `IndSpec`
    71  (`Bridge/Checker/Arms.lean`) is written in run form too (`AM.bind_ok` is its
    72  inversion). -/
    73  @[expose] def PSpec {α : Type} (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) :
    74      Prop :=
    75    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), StateOK s₀ → P s₀.store → c s₀ = .ok (r, s') →
    76      PStep s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Rel.lean#L61-L78
    61  /-! ## The core grade -/
    62  
    63  /-- con-leche: none — **the bridge between the two grades**: a pure step
    64  preserves the whole checking invariant, by `Bridge/StateOK.lean`'s
    65  `CheckOK.mono`.  This is what lets a core-grade function call a pure-grade one
    66  and keep its own hypothesis. -/
    67  theorem PStep.toCore {env : Env} {fe : IFEnv} {s s' : AState}
    68      (h : PStep s s') (hc : CheckOK false env fe s) : CoreStep env fe s s' :=
    69    ⟨hc.monoF h.ok h.ext h.cframe h.pins, h.ext, h.pins⟩

    71  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/Cached/SimC.lean:366 SimC — **the CORE grade's
    72  statement**: the same at a function that calls the knot, so the invariant is
    73  `CheckOK` and the frame is `CoreStep`.  The pure side's fuel existential lives
    74  inside `R`, as `Bridge/Core/Knot.lean`'s `SimE` has it. -/

    76      (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) : Prop :=
    77    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), CheckOK false env fe s₀ → P s₀.store →
    78      c s₀ = .ok (r, s') → CoreStep env fe s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/StructParts.lean#L128-L174
   128  /-! ## The spines -/
   129  
   130  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/StructParts.lean:52-53 structPsAt
   131  The parameter variables as seen from under `o` extra binders.
   132  
   133  **Proof:** a `Nat` recursion over
   134  `internBVarE_run` with the cursor `k` generalised.  The pure side is a
   135  `List.range` map, so the step is `List.range_succ_eq_map` and one `omega` on
   136  the index arithmetic (`k + (j + 1) = k + 1 + j`). -/
   137  theorem structPsAt_go_run (o nP : Nat) : ∀ (n k : Nat) {s s' : AState}
   138      {r : List EIdx}, StateOK s → Arena.structPsAt.go o nP n k s = .ok (r, s') →
   139      PStep s s' ∧ Frontend.denoteEList s'.store r
   140        = some ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j))) := by
   141    intro n
   142    induction n with
   143    | zero =>
   144      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   145      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   146      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok hrun
   147      exact ⟨PStep.refl hok, rfl⟩
   148    | succ n ih =>
   149      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   150      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   151      obtain ⟨b, s₁, h1, h2⟩ := AM.bind_ok hrun
   152      obtain ⟨rest, s₂, h3, h4⟩ := AM.bind_ok h2
   153      obtain ⟨hstep1, hb⟩ := internBVarE_run hok h1
   154      obtain ⟨hstep2, hrest⟩ := ih (k + 1) hstep1.ok h3
   155      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok h4
   156      refine ⟨hstep1.trans hstep2, ?_⟩
   157      have hkey : ((List.range (n + 1)).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j)))
   158          = Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - k) ::
   159            ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + 1 + j))) := by
   160        rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map]
   161        congr 1
   162        refine List.map_congr_left (fun j _ => ?_)
   163        simp only [Function.comp_apply]
   164        congr 1
   165        omega
   166      rw [hkey]
   167      simp only [Frontend.denoteEList, denote_ext hb hstep2.ext, hrest]
   168  
   169  theorem structPsAt_spec (o nP : Nat) :
   170      PSpec PT (Arena.structPsAt o nP) (REL (ConLeche.structPsAt o nP)) := by
   171    intro s₀ s' r hok _ hrun
   172    obtain ⟨hstep, hd⟩ := structPsAt_go_run o nP nP 0 hok hrun
   173    refine ⟨hstep, ?_⟩
   174    simpa only [ConLeche.structPsAt, Nat.zero_add] using hd

    67  theorem knot_spec_all {env : Env} {fe : IFEnv} (henv : ConLeche.EnvWF env) :
    68      ∀ f {eager : Bool}, KnotSpec eager env fe f
    69    | 0, eager => knotSpec_zero eager env fe
    70    | f + 1, _ =>
    71      { whnfCore := fun {c} s₀ d i e hok hden hw =>
    72          memoWhnfCore_step
    73            (fun c => whnfCoreBody_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f) c) (c := c)

    75        whnf := fun s₀ d i e hok hden hw =>
    76          memoWhnf_step henv
    77            (whnfBody_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f)) s₀ d i e hok hden hw
    78        infer := fun s₀ d i e hok hden hw =>
    79          memoInfer_step henv
    80            (inferBody_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f)) s₀ d i e hok hden hw

    82          memoDefeq_step henv

    87            (defeqBody_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f)) s₀ d i j a b hok hda
    88            hdb hwa hwb
    89        inferIO := fun s₀ d i e hok hden hw =>
    90          memoInferIO_step henv
    91            (inferBodyIO_spec henv (knot_spec_all henv f)) s₀ d i e hok hden hw }
