== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L1-L30
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Refine2.Tactic.Lockstep` — the lockstep judgement and the `lockstep` tactic
     3  
     4  Task #97-T2-TACTIC.  Theorem 2 in its lockstep shape (task #97-T2-AUDIT §6)
     5  relates two programs doing the same operations in the same order, over a
     6  state relation that says only "the same data in two representations".  So a
     7  proof of one `_refines` lemma is a ZIP of two do-blocks: peel one bind on each
     8  side, close the correspondence of the two callees with a registered lemma,
     9  continue with the related results.  This file makes that zip a tactic.
    10  
    11  ## The judgement
    12  
    13  `LS pers R m lst x` — *every outcome of the Rust computation `m` is matched by
    14  the twin action `x` run from `lst`*: an `Ok a` by an `ok (b, lst')` with
    15  `R a b` in a related post-state, an `Err e` by the twin throwing at the same
    16  kind (`AErrSim`).  It is `Sim₀` with a relation for the answer instead of an
    17  abstraction function, and with the Rust equation moved into the judgement, so
    18  that the Rust program is visible in the GOAL beside the twin (`LS.toSim₀` is the
    19  bridge back).  Four companion judgements carry the other Rust callee shapes:
    20  
    21  | judgement | Rust callee shape | example |
    22  |---|---|---|
    23  | `LS`  | `Result (Result α CheckError × AState)` — state threaded | `intern_e_app`, a recursive call |
    24  | `LSR` | `Result (Result α CheckError)` — reads, may fail | `view` |
    25  | `LSV` | `Result α` — reads, total | `lift_get`, `inst_list_cutoff` |
    26  | `LSW` | `Result AState` — writes, total | `lift_set` |
    27  | `LSP` | `Result α`, **Rust only** — no twin counterpart | `fuel - 1#u64`, `dup2`, `eidx_nat_key`, `fail` |
    28  | `LSM` | `Result (Result α × AState × M)` — a memoised walk, memo beside the result | `consts_resolve_f_go`, `intern_expr_go` |
    29  | `LSRM` | `Result (Result α × M)` — a memoised reader walk | `all_level_params_defined_go` |
    30  

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L164-L168
   164  /-- **The lockstep judgement** for a state-threading Rust computation. -/
   165  def LS {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   166      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState))
   167      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   168    ∀ o st', m = ok (o, st') → LOut pers R o st' (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L170-L174
   170  /-- A Rust READ that may fail: the state is `st` before and after. -/
   171  def LSR {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   172      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError))
   173      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   174    ∀ o, m = ok o → LOut pers R o st (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L633-L645
   633  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised state walk**: `LS` of the walk with
   634  its memo moved into the answer; `R` relates `(answer, memo)` to the twin's
   635  answer (typically the twin's `(answer, memo)` pair). -/
   636  def LSM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   637      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState × M))
   638      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   639    LS pers R (packM m) lst x
   640  
   641  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised reader walk** at the state `st`. -/
   642  def LSRM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   643      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × M))
   644      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   645    LS pers R (packRM st m) lst x

  2662  macro "lockstep" : tactic => `(tactic| repeat' lockstep_step)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/ExprOps/Mut.lean#L290-L319
   290  theorem instantiate1_go_aux (n : Nat) :
   291      ∀ {pers : arena.store.PersTier} {st : arena.monad.AState} {lst : AState}
   292        (v : arena.handle.EIdx) (fuel : Std.U64) (h : arena.handle.EIdx) (d : Std.U64),
   293        fuel.val = n → AStateRel₀ pers st lst → AStateInv pers st →
   294        LS pers (fun a b => b = absEIdx a) (arena.expr_ops.instantiate1_go pers st v fuel h d) lst
   295          (instantiate1Go (absEIdx v) n (absEIdx h) (absU d)) := by
   296    induction n with
   297    | zero =>
   298      intro pers st lst v fuel h d hn hrel hinv
   299      rw [arena.expr_ops.instantiate1_go, instantiate1Go_zero]
   300      lockstep
   301    | succ m ih =>
   302      intro pers st lst v fuel h d hn hrel hinv
   303      rw [arena.expr_ops.instantiate1_go, instantiate1Go_succ]
   304      lockstep
   305

   307      (v : arena.handle.EIdx) (fuel : Std.U64) (h : arena.handle.EIdx) (d : Std.U64) :
   308      LS pers (fun a b => b = absEIdx a) (arena.expr_ops.instantiate1_go pers st v fuel h d) lst
   309        (instantiate1Go (absEIdx v) (absU fuel) (absEIdx h) (absU d)) :=
   310    instantiate1_go_aux _ v fuel h d rfl hrel hinv
   311  
   312  end instantiate1_go

   316      LS pers (fun a b => b = absEIdx a) (arena.expr_ops.instantiate1_fast pers st fuel e v d) lst
   317        (instantiate1Fast (absU fuel) (absEIdx e) (absEIdx v) (absU d)) := by

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/ExprOps/Mut.lean#L615-L635
   615  theorem inst_spine_from_aux (n : Nat) :
   616      ∀ {pers : arena.store.PersTier} {st : arena.monad.AState} {lst : AState}
   617        (fuel : Std.U64) (args : alloc.vec.Vec arena.handle.EIdx) (i : Std.Usize) (t : Std.U64) (e : arena.handle.EIdx),
   618        args.val.length - i.val = n → AStateRel₀ pers st lst → AStateInv pers st →
   619        LS pers (fun a b => b = absEIdx a) (arena.expr_ops.inst_spine_from pers st fuel args i t e) lst
   620          (instSpine (absU fuel) (absEIdxListFrom args i) (absU t) (absEIdx e)) := by
   621    induction n with
   622    | zero =>
   623      intro pers st lst fuel args i t e hn hrel hinv
   624      rw [arena.expr_ops.inst_spine_from, listFrom_nil args i (by omega), instSpine]
   625      lockstep
   626    | succ k ih =>
   627      intro pers st lst fuel args i t e hn hrel hinv
   628      rw [arena.expr_ops.inst_spine_from, listFrom_cons args i (by omega), instSpine]

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L14-L85
    14  /-!
    15  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    16  
    17  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    18  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    19  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    20  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's headline theorems:
    21  
    22  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — the environment of every stream the Aeneas
    23    model of the Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    24  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    25    type `False` is never accepted by it;
    26  * `no_False_oleans` / `model_exists_oleans` — the same on `--olean`.
    27  
    28  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    29  frontier is measured as their dependency closure, and §5's census prints their
    30  axioms.  What they assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    31  
    32  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    33  
    34  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    35  around the extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    36  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    37  
    38      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    39        → prepare_d → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the check phase)
    40  
    41  **The check phase is the one the binary's driver runs, pool and all**
    42  (`driver::check_decls_driver`): it builds the stream's index from the records
    43  (`stream_index::build_index`), freezes the tier with the index in it
    44  (`checker::freeze_tier`), runs every record's job on `pool::parallel_all`, and
    45  thaws the tier.  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` the index, `h7`
    46  the freeze, `h8` the pool), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles into
    47  `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  `h8` is the contract of the generic
    48  combinator `pool::parallel_all` at the driver's two verified closures (`ParallelAll`
    49  at `jobStep`): index lists, one per worker, covering every job, each in increasing
    50  order, and for each a fold of `run_job` over its indices from `worker_state`,
    51  accepting.  That contract is the pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of
    52  `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.
    53  
    54  The proof:
    55  
    56  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s `…_refines` lemmas walk the Rust runs
    57     into twin runs from the twin's own start state `AState.init EStore.empty`,
    58     related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/`AStateInv`: lockstep); `rust_stages`;
    59  2. **Theorem 1** — `Bridge/Stages.lean` takes the twin runs:
    60     `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` makes the check phase's accept con-leche's pure
    61     fold `checkDeclsPure` accepting the denoted stream at `streamEnv` of it;
    62  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a model,
    63     and `no_proof_of_False_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream.
    64  
    65  ## The named hypotheses
    66  
    67  The headlines start from the binary's own start values (`startState` =
    68  `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`) and name the call the
    69  binary makes at each step.  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    70  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`), what
    71  they assume is exactly:
    72  
    73  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks: the binary
    74    parses with the verified reader loop `parse_source` over the driver's file
    75    handle, and `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
    76    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands out
    77    the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam;
    78  * on `--olean`, `hsnap : SnapshotOf finst fsv F` — the file instance answers as
    79    one snapshot `F`.
    80  
    81  `hpins` is the premise for the binary's pin step: the pin list is what the verified
    82  decoder read, at any text (as con-leche's theorems hold at every pin list);
    83  `model_exists_embedded` / `no_False_declaration_embedded` fix the text to the embedded
    84  `PINS_TEXT`.
    85  -/

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L1-L55
     1  //! `driver` — con-leche's `Driver/{Cli,CheckMain,Run}.lean`, over the ARENA (tasks #37, #48 and
     2  //! #97-P4f), and the Rust side of the Lean twin's
     3  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Main.lean`.
     4  //!
     5  //! The module is that driver in its order: the reads,
     6  //! the index and the check phase with the boundary visible, the `--progress` heartbeat behind
     7  //! one observer trait, the verdict lines, the exit-code mapping, and the flag
     8  //! parsers.  Task #97-SWAP put it here, under the name the shipping driver
     9  //! always had: it was `crates/con-ron-arena/src/driver.rs` through the arena
    10  //! campaign, beside the `Expr`-tree driver it has now replaced, and the
    11  //! eleven representation-free items it used to import across the crate line
    12  //! ([`exit_code`], `verdict_word`, `message`, `ms_secs`, `progress_pace`,
    13  //! `jobs_count`, `default_jobs`, [`workers_for`],
    14  //! `read_up_to`, `STACK_BYTES`) are back in it, unchanged.
    15  //!
    16  //! ## THE EXIT CODES
    17  //!
    18  //! | exit | verdict | meaning |
    19  //! |---|---|---|
    20  //! | 0 | `accepted N declarations` | every declaration checked; `N` counts the file's declaration records |
    21  //! | 1 | `rejected` | a declaration is invalid |
    22  //! | 2 | `declined` | the checker positively detected a feature it does not support, and says which |
    23  //! | 3 | error | bad usage, malformed input, or an internal failure of unclear cause |
    24  //!
    25  //! ## What the arena changed about the driver
    26  //!
    27  //! 1. **The state is one `AState`** (`con_ron_core::arena::monad::AState`: the
    28  //!    store, the per-call memos, the per-declaration caches), threaded as a
    29  //!    `&mut` through the parse, the preparation, the pin walk and the index.
    30  //!    The `Expr`-tree driver threaded a `CState` and the declarations carried
    31  //!    their own terms; here the terms are in the state and the records are
    32  //!    handles into it, so nothing may be run against a state that is not the
    33  //!    one they were interned into.
    34  //! 2. **`intern_all_pins` runs once, before the index, with the scratch tier
    35  //!    off** (DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d, task #97-P4d's "for P4f"): every pinned datum
    36  //!    is in the PERSISTENT cons table before any declaration's check can
    37  //!    intern one into a tier that is about to vanish.  Its result — the
    38  //!    interned pin list — is every job's parameter.
    39  //! 3. **A job's bracket is `record_job`'s**, which empties the scratch tier
    40  //!    around each job.  A driver that checked records itself without it would
    41  //!    grow the scratch tier without bound; the pool calls it once per job and
    42  //!    nothing else opens a tier.
    43  //! 4. **The check phase runs on [`crate::pool`] at every `--jobs=<n>`**, which
    44  //!    is DESIGN.md §8.3's arrangement and needs no atomics: the persistent tier
    45  //!    and the stream's index are immutable once frozen, so they are shared by
    46  //!    reference, and each worker owns a scratch tier, its own caches and a copy
    47  //!    of the pin handles.  `--jobs=1` is the same jobs on one worker.
    48  //!
    49  //! ## The read loop
    50  //!
    51  //! [`parse_export_handle_d`] is `ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean`'s
    52  //! `foldChunks` over forward reads (its positional reads and its parallel
    53  //! rounds parse are not ported): the VERIFIED loop `export_c::parse_source` (task
    54  //! #97-P5-Driver moved it into the core) over [`HandleSource`], the handle
    55  //! read strictly forward 4 MiB at a time, each buffer fed to `chunk_step` and

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L559-L619
   559  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:224-376 checkMainG
   560  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:152-169 checkOleansG
   561  /// `check_decls_driver` with a worker state of the caller's beside each
   562  /// worker's `AState` (`init_x`, one per worker) and the caller's job: an
   563  /// `--olean` run's workers keep the module region they read a theorem's value
   564  /// from (`olean_job`, con-leche's `OleanWorker`), every other run's job is
   565  /// `checker::run_job` with nothing beside it.
   566  pub fn check_decls_driver_with<O, X, I, J>(
   567      pers: &PersTier,
   568      st: &mut AState,
   569      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   570      jobs: u64,
   571      obs: &mut O,
   572      init_x: I,
   573      job: J,
   574  ) -> Result<(), (CheckError, u64)>
   575  where
   576      O: PhaseObserver + Send,
   577      I: Fn() -> X + Sync,
   578      J: Fn(&PersTier, &mut AState, &mut X, u64) -> Result<(), (CheckError, u64)> + Sync,
   579  {
   580      // THE INDEX (the last step of the parse phase): every record's constants and
   581      // tables, a name's first entry winning, read off the records alone.
   582      obs.index_starts();
   583      let ix: IStreamIndex = stream_index::build_index(pers, st, stream_index::stream_index_empty(), ds, 0)?;
   584      obs.parse_done(pers, &st.store, ds.len());
   585      let m = ds.len();
   586      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   587      obs.check_starts(m, workers);
   588      // THE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier and the index leave the state and become
   589      // a value every worker reads.  `st` keeps its (empty) store, its tables
   590      // moved out, so the observer can still read a label back through the tier.
   591      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store, ix);
   592      // THE CHECK PHASE: the job at every record, on `workers` threads, each
   593      // folding it over the jobs it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the verdict and
   594      // the record a rejection names are the one-worker walk's at every `--jobs`.
   595      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   596      let lock: Mutex<(usize, &mut O)> = Mutex::new((0, obs));
   597      let r = parallel_all(
   598          m,
   599          workers,
   600          || (checker::worker_state(&st.pins), init_x()),
   601          |w: &mut (AState, X), k| job(&tier, &mut w.0, &mut w.1, k as u64),
   602          |w: &(AState, X), k| check_line(heartbeat, &lock, &tier, &w.0, m, ds, k),
   603      );
   604      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   605          Ok((_, o)) => o,
   606          Err(e) => e.into_inner().1,
   607      };
   608      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the check — the verdict line's
   609      // declaration label, the failing record's name — reads a handle back out of
   610      // `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has gone out of scope
   611      // answers `None` to every one of them.
   612      let _ix: IStreamIndex = checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   613      let v = pool_verdict(r);
   614      obs.check_done(m, match &v {
   615          Err((_, pos)) => Some(*pos),
   616          Ok(()) => None,
   617      });
   618      v
   619  }

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L50-L102
    50  //! ## THE TRUSTED CLAIM, and the whole of it
    51  //!
    52  //! **If `parallel_all(n, workers, init, step, after)` returns `Ok(())`, then
    53  //! every index in `0..n` was claimed by some worker; each worker built its
    54  //! state with `init()` exactly once and folded `step` over the indices it
    55  //! claimed, in claim order, which is increasing; and every one of those
    56  //! `step` calls returned `Ok(())`** — at every worker count.  That is
    57  //! `ParallelAll` in `proof/ConRon/Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean` (task
    58  //! #98-POOL; the increasing order added at task #143), and it is a statement
    59  //! about this module's control flow only — nothing about what `init` and
    60  //! `step` compute.  With the driver's closures it is the capstone's pool
    61  //! premise: index lists covering `0..ds.len`, each increasing, and for each
    62  //! list a fold of `run_job` over it from `worker_state pins`, accepting,
    63  //! which the proof relates, worker by worker, to the twin
    64  //! (`pool_accepts_refines`).
    65  //!
    66  //! The claim is weaker than what the code does: the counter below hands each
    67  //! index to exactly ONE worker, but the contract does not promise that — the
    68  //! proof needs coverage and each worker's increasing order, nothing about
    69  //! repetition across workers.  The argument:
    70  //!
    71  //! * **A claim is a `fetch_add` on one counter.**  Each value `0, 1, 2, …` is
    72  //!   handed to exactly one caller, so every index in `0..n` is claimed (by
    73  //!   exactly one worker, in fact).  A worker stops at its first claim `≥ n`.
    74  //! * **A worker's claims increase.**  The counter only grows, so each
    75  //!   `fetch_add` a worker makes returns more than the one before it: the
    76  //!   order a worker steps its indices in is increasing.
    77  //! * **A worker is one fold.**  `worker` calls `init()` once, then for each
    78  //!   claimed index `k` calls `step(&mut st, k)` on that one state — the fold,
    79  //!   in claim order.  `after(&st, k)` sees the state by `&` only.  A claimed
    80  //!   index at or above `limit` is skipped without a call, and on an accepting
    81  //!   run the limit never moves (only a failing step lowers it), so no claimed
    82  //!   index is skipped.
    83  //! * **Merge by index — master's argument.**  A worker hands back each index
    84  //!   it stepped with the step's result; the workers' arrays are merged *by
    85  //!   index* into one table and `first_failure` walks it in index order,
    86  //!   answering `Ok` only if every slot holds `Ok`.  So an accept means every
    87  //!   index was stepped, successfully, by the worker that claimed it, whatever
    88  //!   the timing.  An empty slot is `ParallelError::Missing`, never `Ok`.
    89  //!
    90  //! The failure side is not part of the claim the capstone uses, but the pool
    91  //! keeps master's behaviour there: the walk stops at the first failing index,
    92  //! and the table is complete below it.  con-leche's argument: a worker whose
    93  //! step fails at `f` lowers the shared `limit` to `f`, and a worker skips a
    94  //! claimed index at or above the limit.  Every value the limit ever holds is
    95  //! `n` or a *failing* index, hence at least the first failing index `f`; so an
    96  //! index below `f` is never skipped, and — the counter being monotone — it was
    97  //! claimed before `f` was and is finished by the worker that claimed it.
    98  //! `pool_reports_the_first_failure_at_every_jobs` is the test, at 1, 2, 3, 4
    99  //! and 8 workers on a list whose records 2 and 4 both fail;
   100  //! `pool_is_the_one_worker_walk_at_every_jobs` checks that the check phase's verdict
   101  //! is the one-worker walk's; `parallel_all_partitions_the_indices` checks the
   102  //! claim itself on a state that records its claims.

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Checker/Jobs.lean#L170-L174
   170  def ParallelAll {S E : Type} (n : Nat) (init : Result S)
   171      (step : S → Nat → Result (core.result.Result Unit E × S)) : Prop :=
   172    ∃ parts : List (List Nat),
   173      (∀ k < n, ∃ w ∈ parts, k ∈ w) ∧
   174      ∀ w ∈ parts, w.Pairwise (· < ·) ∧ ∃ s₀, init = ok s₀ ∧ FoldAllOk step s₀ w

== scripts/gates.sh#L6-L36
     6  # Runs, in order, and stops at the first failure:
     7  #   1. cargo build                          the crate compiles, warning-free
     8  #   2. cargo test                           the unit tests pass
     9  #   3. scripts/lint-rust-style.sh           the Aeneas subset (§3.4), both crates
    10  #      scripts/dead-rust.py --check         no `pub` Rust item without a caller
    11  #                                           (task #105)
    12  #   4. scripts/provenance.py check          every item cites con-leche (§3.7)
    13  #      scripts/pin-last.py                  no commit but the tip moves the
    14  #                                           con-leche pin (§7, task #108)
    15  #   5. scripts/provenance-selftest.py        the gate's Lean parser and the
    16  #                                           bump classifier, on their fixtures
    17  #   6. scripts/twin-lines.py check          every `Lean twin:` line names a
    18  #                                           declaration of `proof/ConRon/**` at
    19  #                                           its current lines (§3.7)
    20  #   7. scripts/overview-links.sh            OVERVIEW.md/DESIGN.md line anchors
    21  #   8. scripts/holes.sh --check             OVERVIEW.md §8.1 == the model's holes
